title: DR1 offers ten animal-approved border control posts as the port of exit; the frontend offers the whole 78-entry list of GB ports and airports, most of which cannot handle live animals.

finding.frontend: The Port of exit select lists 78 entries from Aberdeen Airport (GB DYC) to Tilbury Port (GB TILL) — every general GB port and airport, including places with no animal facilities such as Cambridge Airport and Nottingham Port. The options come from the ports-of-entry list, which the page reuses wholesale: src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/port-of-exit/controller.js:22-30 maps ports.list(), and src/server/app/services/ports/index.js:11 fills that from the reference-data service's /ports-of-entry endpoint. The hint says so out loud — "Choose where the consignment will leave Great Britain. Exit and entry share the same port list." — at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/port-of-exit/copy/copy.en.js:5. The same 78-entry select is offered for transit and for temporary admission horses alike, and validation accepts any code in it: :32-38.
finding.prototype: The Port of exit select offers ten options and each names the site and its animal BCP code, quoted here exactly as DR1 renders them: "Edinburgh Airport (animals) - GBEDI4", "Gatwick Airport (animals) - GBLGW4", "Glasgow Airport (animals) - GBGLA002", "Heathrow Airport - HARC (animals) - GBLHR4A", "Heathrow Airport – Airpets Limited (animals) – GBLHR022 - GBLHR022", "Heathrow Airport – Animal Aircare Ltd (animals) - GBLHR067", "Holyhead POE - GBHLY", "Manchester Airport (animals) - GBMNC4", "Prestwick Airport (animals) - GBPIK4" and "Stansted Airport (animals) - GBSTN4A". The Airpets entry repeats its code twice and three entries separate their parts with an en dash where the other seven use a hyphen; both are in DR1's own data, so whoever builds the real list should treat those two as DR1 errors to be tidied rather than copied. The same ten are offered under Transit and under Temporary admission horses. There is no hint on the field.
finding.difference: The exit port must be chosen from the animal-approved border control posts, not from the ports-of-entry list. Reference data has no such list today — the frontend's only source is /ports-of-entry — so a list of exit BCPs has to exist there first, keyed on the animal BCP codes DR1 shows, and the port-of-exit page then reads that instead of ports.list(). The hint sentence "Exit and entry share the same port list" goes with it, since it will no longer be true. Until reference data carries the list this cannot be finished in the frontend alone. Note also that DR1 labels each option with its BCP code, which the frontend's "(GB XXX)" suffix does not carry.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a second, animal-restricted port list behind the frontend's port-of-exit page — the controller calls ports.list() with no filter, that list is the /ports-of-entry response, and neither "border control post" nor "BCP" appears anywhere in src/server/app.
finding.verification: Counted the options in fe-port-of-exit's rendered DOM: 80 elements, being the placeholder "Select port of exit", a disabled divider and 78 ports running from "Aberdeen Airport (GB DYC)" to "Tilbury Port (GB TILL)". Confirmed "Cambridge Airport (GB CBG)" and "Nottingham Port (GB NTG)" are both offered. Extracted the ten exit options from dr1-reason-for-import-transit-revealed and compared them against app/data/exit-border-control-posts.js line by line. Read the transit and temporary-admission reveals in dr1-reason-for-import.html and confirmed both draw the same ten and neither carries a hint. Re-resolved every citation: port-of-exit/controller.js:22-30 is portItems mapping ports.list() unfiltered, :32-38 is the requiredOneOf built from the same unfiltered list, services/ports/index.js:11 is `ports = await fetchPortsOfEntry()`, and copy.en.js:5 is the hint string verbatim. Checked the band rather than accepting it: services/ports/client.js fetches /ports-of-entry from the reference-data service and there is no second endpoint, so `needs-backend` holds. Ran the falsifier: grep -rniE "border.control|\bBCP\b" over src/server/app returns two hits, both "border control checks" in the declaration copy, and no port list. Rubric 6 checked — DR1 does not itself offer a general port list here, so this is not asking the frontend to fix something DR1 also does. CORRECT apart from one quotation.
finding.correction: Claimed, in the prototype slot: "Heathrow Airport – Airpets Limited (animals) – GBLHR022". DR1 does not render that. Both the captured DOM and app/data/exit-border-control-posts.js:8 carry "Heathrow Airport – Airpets Limited (animals) – GBLHR022 - GBLHR022", with the BCP code repeated. The author tidied DR1's own data error away instead of reporting it, which is the one thing quote conservation forbids: the requirements side's mistake is part of the requirement and whoever builds the reference-data list needs to see it before deciding whether to reproduce it. The slot now quotes all ten verbatim and names both DR1 data defects — the doubled code, and the en dashes in three entries against hyphens in the other seven. Separately, the falsifier said "border control post" appears nowhere "outside the declaration copy", which overstates the exception: the exact phrase appears nowhere at all, and what the declaration copy holds is "border control checks". Falsifier tightened. Neither change affects the finding's substance or its band.
